claims.text: NWS Indianapolis's dedicated 'Record Flooding of August 2026' page states that from 11-17 August 2026 repeated rounds of thunderstorms brought rainfall totals 'over a foot' in places, with the highest amounts 'east of Indy with over 12 inches recorded'; it reports the White River at Anderson crested at 24.93 feet on 8/14/2026, surpassing the previous all-time record of 23.60 feet set in 1913, and at Noblesville crested at 24.60 feet on 8/15/2026, also surpassing its 1913 record of 23.80 feet; the White River at Nora reached 21.18 feet on 8/15/2026, the highest level since the 1913 record. The page also states a 58-year-old woman and her dog died on 8/14/2026 after driving into floodwaters near Yorktown.

The State of Indiana's own event announcement confirms that Governor Mike Braun declared a Statewide Disaster Emergency on Thursday, 13 August 2026, 'in response to widespread damage, power outages and flooding caused by this week's severe storms and derecho,' directing state agencies to coordinate emergency response across Franklin, Henry, Lake, LaPorte, Madison, Newton, Porter and Pulaski counties (Executive Order 26-21), and authorizing deployment of Indiana National Guard troops to Gary, Munster and Hobart for life-saving activities as well as cleanup and support.

description: Repeated rounds of severe thunderstorms and a derecho crossed Indiana between 11 and 17 August 2026, dropping over a foot of rain in places -- the heaviest totals, over 12 inches, east of Indianapolis -- and driving the White River to record levels. NWS Indianapolis recorded the river cresting at Anderson at 24.93 feet on 14 August, surpassing the all-time record of 23.60 feet set in 1913, and at Noblesville at 24.60 feet on 15 August, past that gauge's 1913 record of 23.80 feet; at Nora it reached 21.18 feet, its highest level since 1913. One death is confirmed: a 58-year-old woman and her dog died on 14 August after driving into floodwaters near Yorktown, though wider media reporting has described a higher statewide toll from the same storm system that no authoritative source has corroborated. Governor Mike Braun declared a Statewide Disaster Emergency on 13 August under Executive Order 26-21, covering eight counties from Franklin and Henry to Porter and Pulaski, and ordered Indiana National Guard troops to Gary, Munster and Hobart for life-saving work as well as cleanup and support; the storm sequence ended on 17 August and the response has moved to cleanup.

impact.summary: NWS Indianapolis's event page confirms one death -- a 58-year-old woman and her dog, who drove into floodwaters near Yorktown on 14 August 2026 -- after rainfall of over 12 inches east of Indianapolis drove the White River to record crests at Anderson (24.93 feet, past the 23.60-foot record set in 1913) and Noblesville (24.60 feet, past 23.80 feet in 1913). Governor Mike Braun declared a Statewide Disaster Emergency on 13 August 2026 under Executive Order 26-21 for eight counties and deployed the Indiana National Guard to Gary, Munster and Hobart.
